Project Proposal and Plan Report

University capstone projects require students to work with information from multiple sources, including general capstone guidance, project briefs, proposals, sponsor requirements, meeting outcomes, milestones, and other project documentation. As projects progress, this information can become distributed across different documents and communication channels, making it difficult for students and other project stakeholders to quickly locate and interpret information relevant to a particular project activity.
The broader opportunity is an AI-assisted capstone project management system that could progressively support capstone project activities through AI-assisted access to project information and project-management functionality. However, developing the entire system is outside the boundaries of this current project. The project, therefore, focuses on a specific Micro-SaaS module: an AI-assisted Capstone Project Assistant.
The Capstone Assistant will provide a central conversational interface through which authorized users can interact with both general capstone information and contextual information belonging to specific projects.

focuses on a specific Micro-SaaS module: an AI-assisted Capstone Project Assistant.
The Capstone Assistant will provide a central conversational interface through which authorized users can interact with both general capstone information and contextual information belonging to specific projects. It will provide two related forms of assistance:
General capstone assistance, using approved general capstone information.
Project-specific assistance, using information associated with an authorized capstone project, including project documents, meetings, milestones, and basic project information.
Trellis Data's sovereign Agentaus AI will be used for natural-language response generation.
As the project involves the practical integration of a Large Language Model (LLM), the prototype will also address key applied-AI considerations identified in the sponsor brief, including prompt design and refinement, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and evaluation of AI response accuracy, latency, and usability. These considerations will be incorporated into the design, testing, and monitoring of the prototype.
The Micro-SaaS is intended to reduce the effort required to locate, interpret, and use relevant capstone and project information. The current project therefore focuses specifically on information access and contextual AI assistance, rather than attempting to implement the entire future AI-assisted capstone project management system.

The primary outcome will be a functional prototype of a Capstone Assistant demonstrating how sovereign AI can assist users with both general Capstone information and contextual information relating to individual Capstone projects.
The project is expected to deliver:
A functional web-based Micro-SaaS prototype.
Role-appropriate access to Capstone projects.
General Capstone conversational assistance.
Project-specific conversational assistance.
Essential project information through documents, meetings and milestones.
Grounded AI responses using relevant retrieved information.
An iteratively tested and refined prototype.
A simple Administrator dashboard demonstrating monitoring of AI usage, response latency, failures, user feedback and evaluation results.
An evaluated AI assistant demonstrating prompt refinement, hallucination mitigation and measurable response quality.

The objectives are to:
Design and develop a focused AI-assisted Capstone Project Assistant.
Improve access to general Capstone information.
Provide contextual assistance using authorised project information.
support different project-access requirements for Students, Mentors and the Convenor.
Integrate Trellis Data Agentaus AI for response generation.
Reduce unsupported AI responses through controlled retrieval and fallback behaviour.
Test and progressively improve the Micro-SaaS through iterative prompt refinement, system testing and user feedback during the project delivery period.
Evaluate AI response quality, latency and usability using defined evaluation measures.
Provide simple monitoring capabilities that allow the Administrator to review AI and system performance.

1. Users will have an identifiable system role.
Each user will operate as a Student, Mentor, Convenor or Administrator so that appropriate functionality and project access can be provided.
2. Students should access only projects to which they belong.
Project documents and project-specific information should not automatically be accessible to members of unrelated projects.
3. Mentors should access only their assigned teams.
Mentors require contextual information about the teams they support without requiring access to unrelated projects.
4. The Convenor requires visibility across all Capstone projects.
The Convenor requires broader project oversight than Students and Mentors.
5. General and project-specific information should remain logically separated.
General Capstone guidance applies across projects, whereas sponsor decisions, project requirements and meeting outcomes relate to individual projects.
6. AI assistance remains advisory.
Capstone Assistant assists users in accessing information but does not replace formal advice or stakeholder judgement (Human in the loop).
7. AI performance can be evaluated using a representative test set.
A defined set of general and project-specific Capstone questions will be used to evaluate response relevance, grounded accuracy, hallucination occurrence and response latency during prototype testing.
8. Agentaus AI will remain available during prototype development, testing, deployment and future development.

Key assumptions will be validated through sponsor and mentor discussions, stakeholder feedback and prototype demonstrations.
Attention will be given to the role-access assumptions. Prototype scenarios will test whether Students see only their projects, Mentors see only their assigned teams and the Convenor can access all projects.

The performance of Capstone Assistant will be evaluated using a predefined set of representative general and project-specific Capstone questions. The evaluation will assess response relevance, grounded accuracy, hallucination occurrence, response latency and user-perceived usefulness. Questions for which sufficient information is deliberately unavailable will also be included to evaluate whether the assistant applies the intended fallback behaviour rather than generating unsupported information.
Prompt configurations will be refined iteratively during development. Results obtained using an initial prompt configuration will be compared with subsequent prompt versions to determine whether prompt changes improve response quality and reduce unsupported outputs. Agentaus interaction latency, request success or failure, user feedback and selected evaluation results will be recorded and summarised through the Administrator AI and System Performance Dashboard.

4. Brief Justification of the Chosen Option/Method
4.1 Proposed Solution
The chosen solution is a web-based AI-assisted Capstone Project Assistant developed as a focused Micro-SaaS prototype. The system will provide authorised Students, Mentors, the Convenor and Administrator with a conversational interface for accessing relevant Capstone information.
The assistant will support two main types of interaction:
General Capstone assistance, using approved general Capstone information; and
Project-specific assistance, using authorised project information such as project documents, meetings, milestones and basic project details.
Trellis Data's Agentaus AI will be used for natural-language response generation. Rather than allowing the AI to answer solely from general model knowledge, the application will retrieve relevant information and provide it as context to Agentaus. This approach is intended to improve response relevance and reduce unsupported or hallucinated information.
The prototype will also include configurable prompt templates, prompt version tracking, user feedback and AI performance monitoring so that the quality of the assistant can be evaluated and progressively improved during development.
4.2 Justification of the Selected Approach
The selected approach was chosen because the main problem identified in the project is not the absence of project-management software, but the difficulty of quickly locating and interpreting relevant information distributed across Capstone guidance, project documents, meeting records, milestones and other project artefacts.
A conversational AI assistant provides users with a natural-language method of accessing this information without requiring them to manually search through multiple documents.

The proposed solution is also suitable for the project's 10-week development period because it focuses on a specific Micro-SaaS module rather than attempting to develop the complete future Capstone project-management platform.
Another important reason for selecting this approach is the opportunity to investigate practical applied-AI challenges. The project can evaluate not only whether Agentaus generates a response, but whether the response is relevant, grounded in retrieved information, avoids unsupported claims and is returned within an acceptable response time.
4.3 Retrieval Method
Three retrieval approaches were considered for identifying relevant information before sending context to Agentaus:

TF-IDF with cosine similarity has been selected as the preferred retrieval method for the prototype.
This method provides sufficient retrieval capability for a controlled collection of Capstone and project documents while remaining lightweight and explainable.

TF-IDF with cosine similarity has been selected as the preferred retrieval method for the prototype.
This method provides sufficient retrieval capability for a controlled collection of Capstone and project documents while remaining lightweight and explainable. It also avoids introducing vector-database and embedding infrastructure that may add unnecessary complexity within the 10-week project period.
Vector retrieval will remain a potential future enhancement if prototype evaluation demonstrates that TF-IDF retrieval is insufficient.
4.4 Data Storage Method
JSON, SQLite and PostgreSQL were considered for storing system information.
SQLite has been selected as the preferred database for the prototype because it provides relational data storage while remaining lightweight and simple to deploy. Relational storage is useful for maintaining relationships between users, roles, projects, meetings, milestones and project access.
JSON alone would provide simpler initial development but is less suitable for managing relational user and project-access requirements. PostgreSQL would provide greater production scalability but introduces additional deployment complexity that is unnecessary for the current Micro-SaaS prototype.
4.5 User Interface Approach
A browser-based interface will be used because the system is intended to support multiple user roles and provide access without requiring desktop software installation.
For the MVP, rapid development will be prioritised over advanced interface customisation.

4.5 User Interface Approach
A browser-based interface will be used because the system is intended to support multiple user roles and provide access without requiring desktop software installation.
For the MVP, rapid development will be prioritised over advanced interface customisation. A lightweight web framework such as Streamlit may therefore be used where appropriate because it supports rapid development of AI-based prototypes and can provide the required conversational interface, project selection and administrative views within the available project timeframe.
A fully customised front-end and back-end architecture provides greater interface flexibility but requires significantly greater development effort. This may be considered for future development if the prototype is expanded into a production system.
4.6 Prompt Engineering and Grounding Approach
Structured prompt templates will be developed separately for general Capstone assistance and project-specific assistance.
For a general Capstone question, the application will retrieve relevant approved general Capstone information and provide that information to Agentaus as context.
For a project-specific question, the application will first confirm that the user is authorised to access the selected project and will retrieve information only from that project.
Where appropriate, general and project-specific information may be combined.

User Question
→ Identify User and Role
→ Determine General or Project Context
→ Check Project Authorisation
→ Retrieve Relevant Information
→ Construct Prompt
→ Agentaus AI
→ Generate Grounded Response
→ Record Performance Information and Feedback

If sufficient information cannot be retrieved, the assistant will provide appropriate fallback guidance rather than intentionally generating unsupported information.
4.7 Alternatives Considered
A general-purpose chatbot without controlled retrieval was considered but was not selected because it would provide less control over the information used to answer Capstone questions and could increase the likelihood of generic or unsupported responses.
A complete Capstone project-management system was also considered. However, implementing task allocation, advanced scheduling, risk-management workflows, automated analytics and other comprehensive project-management functionality would significantly increase the project scope and would not be realistic within the current 10-week development period.
A vector-database-based retrieval architecture was considered but has been deferred because the additional embedding and vector infrastructure is not currently necessary for demonstrating the core concept.
The selected approach therefore provides an appropriate balance between functionality, technical complexity, AI experimentation and the available development timeframe.

General Capstone conversational assistance.
Project-specific conversational assistance.
Basic project profiles and project selection.

The project team will be responsible for day-to-day planning, development, integration, testing and documentation.
